Canada-EU Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally in force 21 September 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal AML/CFT: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 83.02 and 462.31; FINTRAC interpretive guidance on beneficial ownership and politically exposed persons. Sanctions framework: Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 21. Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1 and its Regulation; Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2186-2249 (societe en commandite); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11. Tax/UBO interplay: Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.); Taxation Act, CQLR c. I-3.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the general partner's home jurisdiction (e.g., State Administration for Market Regulation, PRC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 HCCH Convention; effective for Canada 11 January 2024 and for the PRC 7 November 2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the foreign general partner's certificate of incorporation and articles (or equivalent constitutive instrument)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent incorporation authority of the general partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Consular Legalization only if the home state is not an HCCH 1961 member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board of directors / equity holders resolution authorizing the formation of the Quebec limited partnership and the capital commitment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the foreign general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in home jurisdiction + Hague Apostille + certified French translation by an OATIAQ-certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney / mandate appointing the Quebec-based resident agent (mandataire) for service of process and regulatory filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign general partner (duly acting through its authorized officers)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization + Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-HCCH jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO identification kit: valid passport copies, proof of residential address, ownership chain chart, and executed PEP self-declaration for each ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Individual ultimate beneficial owners and the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification of true copies + Hague Apostille where the underlying record originates outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement evidencing the initial contribution to the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized execution by the account officer; apostille or consular legalization only upon FINTRAC, REQ, or Revenu Quebec demand

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at formation and on an ongoing basis against: (1) UN Security Council Consolidated List (Resolutions 1267/1988 and 1989 regimes); (2) Canadian domestic sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky); (3) OSFI consolidated sanctions dashboard; (4) FINTRAC prescribed PEP indicators and the PCMLTFA beneficial-ownership definition; and (5) OFAC SDN list as a prudential benchmark for USD Swift_TT clearing and Platform_Pay settlement. All screening results, source-of-funds records, and CDD files must be archived for a minimum of five years and made available to FINTRAC or Revenu Quebec upon demand.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11): every Quebec business name must have a mandatory French version for use in contracts, invoices, and signage; a name originating in a non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese) must be transliterated into Latin characters and joined by a French version of equal prominence; the legal name of a limited partnership must terminate with 'Societe en commandite' (S.E.C.) or 'Limited Partnership' (L.P.).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms requiring prior ministerial or regulatory authorization: Bank/Banque, Trust/Fiduciaire, Assurance/Insurance, University/Universite, College, Ordre, Chambre, Bourse, Courtier/Broker
Terms suggesting Crown, state, or governmental connection: Royal, Imperial, Federal, Canada/Canadien, Quebec (when implying public authority), Police, RCMP/Gendarmerie
Legal-form tokens inconsistent with an S.E.C./L.P.: Corporation, Inc., Corp., Ltd., S.A., or any word suggesting a joint-stock company or unlimited partner status

Terms that are obscene, contemptuous, defamatory, or likely to mislead the public within the meaning of the Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The REQ name reservation is valid for 90 days; renewal is possible by filing a new reservation application and paying the tariff before expiry (no automatic extension). Upon rejection, counsel may: (1) request an administrative review by the Registrar under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises within 30 days of the written refusal; (2) if the refusal is maintained, appeal the decision to the Court of Quebec within 30 days of notification; and (3) in parallel, resubmit an amended name that remedies the Registrar's stated objections, which constitutes the most expedient practical path.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted: a registered-office service address at a genuine physical location in Quebec is acceptable for receipt of legal process and registry correspondence, but a P.O. box or pure mail-forwarding virtual office is statutorily insufficient. For the ISIC 4646 wholesale activity, the limited partnership must maintain real commercial substance in Quebec, including books and records, a Quebec bank account, and evidence of management functions carried on by the general partner or its local agent, to preserve pass-through treatment and access to treaty benefits under the Income Tax Act and the Taxation Act.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5% annual probability). FINTRAC and Revenu Quebec generally do not conduct unannounced on-site inspections for standard low-risk wholesale distributors of optical goods; physical verification is most likely to arise incidentally in the course of a GST/QST audit, a payroll compliance review, or a named-beneficiary quality assurance check.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), Book Five, Title Five — Partnership, arts. 2186 et seq., including arts. 2236–2248 applicable to the limited partnership (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 6–21, 29–33 and 41–44 (declaration, registration, and legal publicity of the limited partnership); Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises for prescribed forms and fees (CQLR c. P-44.1).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Quebec Enterprise Registrar; online filing through the cliquer portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca) and regional offices in Montréal, Québec City, and other administrative centres.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de société en commandite (Declaration of Limited Partnership) filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required for a Québec limited partnership (Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236–2248). Limited partners must contribute money or property, not services; general partners may contribute capital, property, or services. No escrow, bank attestation, or capital deposit is mandated. The Declaration of Limited Partnership must state the contribution of each limited partner and, for general partners, describe their contribution or obligation to contribute; where required, the partnership agreement fixes capital accounts and distribution entitlements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BY WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER, adopted effective as of [date], IT IS RESOLVED: (1) that the Partnership accepts the capital contribution and the limited partner subscription tendered under the Partnership Agreement and fixes contributed capital at [amount]; (2) that the registered office be located at [address], Province of Québec, Canada; (3) that [Name] be and is hereby appointed Manager and chief representative, with authority to execute registrations with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and Revenu Québec, open bank accounts, and instruct counsel; and (4) that the Manager perfect all legal publicity, municipal permits, and occupational registrations. This Resolution is effective immediately and remains in force unless revoked in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Availability search and reservation of the limited partnership name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online enterprise register search and name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search of the REQ online register to verify that the proposed distinctive name of the limited partnership does not conflict with an existing registered enterprise, reserved name, or trademark. If desired, file a Request for Reservation of Name through the cliquer portal; the name must contain a distinctive element and, if used, a legal designation such as 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.'. The reservation is valid for 90 days and renewable.
required_dossiers: Online name search extraction or report
Request for Reservation of Name (if used)
Identification particulars of the general partner submitting the request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, the general partner may submit an amended requisition within 30 days, add distinguishing numerals or initials, or request reconsideration by REQ; a corrected name search and re-filing under the same declaration file complete the cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partners and limited partners, assisted by a Québec notary or transactional attorney; the instrument is private and not filed with any government register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a partnership agreement defining the partnership name, registered office in Québec, purpose (wholesale international distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames — ISIC 4646 / NAICS 423460), contributions and capital accounts, profit-sharing, management authority of the general partner, withdrawal and transfer conditions, and dispute resolution. The agreement must conform to Civil Code of Québec arts. 2186–2200 and 2236–2248. No notarial deed is required unless real property is contributed.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite)
Schedule A — contribution statements of general and limited partners
Schedule B — identity documents (passport or Québec-issued ID) of all partners
Power of attorney or signing mandate where the general partner acts through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Ambiguities in contribution, management, or profit-sharing clauses are cured by a supplemental agreement (avenant) executed by all partners; if a partner withdraws before filing, the contribution schedules are restated and re-executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Limited Partnership (Déclaration de société en commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — cliquer online filing portal and counters of the Société québécoise d'information juridique / REQ service points
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Declaration of Limited Partnership through the REQ cliquer platform. Enter the general partner's legal name and domicile, the partnership name, the principal business activity (wholesale of opaque optical frames and ophthalmic eyewear goods), the registered office address in Québec, the contribution of each limited partner, and the names of partners liable to third parties. Pay the prescribed filing fee by credit card or bank transfer. Upon approval, REQ issues the Québec enterprise number (NEQ) and the attestation of legal publicity.
required_dossiers: Duly completed Declaration of Limited Partnership (REQ form prescribed under CQLR c. P-44.1)
Proof of identity of the general partner or authorized representative (two pieces of ID for counter filings)
Certified extract or copy of the partnership agreement or contribution schedule, if attached
Payment of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of refusal or incompleteness, the general partner may remedy within the stated period (usually 10–30 days) by filing the missing declarations or an amending requisition; failure to remedy leads to cancellation of the declaration, after which a new filing and fee are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Québec tax registrations (CRA Business Number and Revenu Québec accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO); Revenu Québec — integrated enterprise registration services (cliquez)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ issued by REQ, register for the federal Business Number (BN) and, as applicable, the GST/HST account; register with Revenu Québec for QST (TVQ) collection, given the Québec registered office and wholesale activities, and for payroll source deductions if employees are hired. Because the limited partnership is a pass-through entity, net income is reported on partnership returns (CRA T5013 and Revenu Québec Relevé 15) allocated to partners; registration at the partnership level covers remittance and compliance obligations.
required_dossiers: NEQ attestation issued by REQ
Extract of the Declaration of Limited Partnership
Limited partnership agreement (for pass-through classification review)
Principal representative's identification and Social Insurance Number or Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registration discrepancies are corrected online by amending the CRA/Revenu Québec account profiles; if a T5013 or Relevé 15 filing deadline is missed, voluntary disclosure under the CRA Voluntary Disclosures Program or Revenu Québec's equivalent may reduce penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal operating permit (permis d'exploitation / licence de commerce)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of the registered office and warehouse (e.g., Ville de Montréal — Service des permis et inspections; Ville de Québec — Service de l'urbanisme et du développement économique)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business permit covering commercial warehousing and wholesale distribution of optical goods. Submit the REQ attestation, identification of the legal representative, and proof of occupancy rights under the lease. The permitting service verifies zoning conformity for warehouse and wholesale activity, building occupancy classification, municipal fire safety requirements, and any signage permit requirement. Fees are set by municipal tariff.
required_dossiers: REQ attestation of legal publicity (extrait du registre)
Municipal business permit application form
Commercial lease or proof of right of occupancy
Fire safety conformity attestation or inspection letter, where requested
Zoning certificate or land-use verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit application is refused, the applicant may request administrative review before the municipal permit committee, amend the premises plans or zoning application, or seek a minor variance before the city planning advisory committee; certain municipal permit decisions may be appealed to the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening, capital contribution deposit, and occupational/insurance closings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chosen Canadian chartered bank or credit union (e.g., BMO, RBC, National Bank, Desjardins); Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a commercial operating bank account in the partnership's name using the REQ attestation and the pro-forma resolution. Deposit the capital contributions reflected in the Declaration and record them in the partnership's capital accounts. If the partnership hires staff, register the employer file with CNESST for occupational health and safety coverage and obtain general liability and warehouse property insurance. Confirm the registered office address with the bank and all government registers.
required_dossiers: Certificate of legal publicity (attestation REQ)
Declaration of Limited Partnership and partnership agreement
Pro-forma resolution appointing the Manager
Identification of the Manager or principal representative
General liability and property insurance certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional KYC clearance, provide a certified enterprise excerpt, the general partner's resolution, and source-of-funds declarations; if CNESST registration is disputed, file a rectification request and register retroactively upon proof of coverage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No province-specific industrial manufacturing licence applies to wholesale distribution. General oversight rests with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec for legal publicity and the local municipal permits service for commercial occupancy; the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie provides sectoral guidance only.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis d'exploitation commerciale / municipal operating permit for commercial warehousing and wholesale (where a Québec premises is operated); no sectoral industrial operation permit under the Québec industrial licensing regime applies to wholesale of opthalmic eyewear frames.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Bureau des évaluations environnementales (BEE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category C / no environmental authorization required: wholesale warehousing and distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames do not constitute a mandatorily assessable 'project' under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment of certain projects (CQLR c. Q-2) or the Regulation respecting environmental authorization and declaration of certain activities (CQLR c. Q-2). No EIA study, certificate of authorization, or attestation is required for a non-manufacturing storage and distribution use below regulatory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams arise from the wholesale storage and distribution of acetate eyeglass frames. Stormwater and sanitary sewer discharges remain subject to municipal sewer bylaws and applicable industrial discharge limits (e.g., municipal Régiement sur les rejets industriels dans les réseaux d'égout); air emissions are negligible for sealed packaged goods and must respect provincial ambient air quality standards under CQLR c. Q-2. Cardboard and plastic packaging waste must be recovered or recycled under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of residual materials (CQLR c. Q-2) and municipal waste management rules; refrigerant, PCB, or VOC-containing equipment thresholds do not apply to premises without manufacturing or large refrigeration systems.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification per the Règlement sur la sécurité incendie under the Act respecting fire safety (CQLR c. S-3.4) and municipal fire code inspections for storage occupancy; structural load and building occupancy classification conformity under the Québec Construction Code, Chapter I — Building (CQLR c. B-1.1) for any leasehold improvements, including municipal building permits where required; CNESST employer registration and workplace compliance under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c. S-2.1) for storage personnel; emergency measures, fire extinguisher servicing, and general liability insurance maintained as part of the operating permit.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal GST/HST, excise and federal income tax administration; portals: CRA My Business Account and CRA Business Registration Online (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). Revenu Québec — Québec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec income tax and provincial tax accounts; portal: Revenu Québec My Account for Businesses (revenuquebec.ca). Registration of extra-provincial limited partnerships: Registraire d'entreprises du Québec (REQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Canadian or extra-provincial Quebec limited partnership: (1) First complete any required registration with the Registraire d'entreprises du Québec if the LP carries on business in Quebec; for a non-Quebec LP, file for extra-provincial recognition. (2) Obtain a CRA Business Number by using Business Registration Online or Form RC1, and add the GST/HST program account (BN plus 'RT' suffix) for deemed or mandatory registration. (3) Register with Revenu Québec through its business registration portal or application form, requesting a QST account, after establishing commercial activity in Quebec or filing a voluntary registration. (4) Provide the governing LP agreement, certificate of extra-provincial registration and authorization documents executed by the general partner. (5) Open any required import/export account with the CBSA and, if the LP has Quebec employees, payroll program accounts with CRA and Revenu Québec. No Canadian federal incorporation is required to obtain a tax identity; a foreign entity may register directly in the name of the LP through its authorized representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — tax-transparent for Canadian federal and Quebec income tax purposes; income is allocated to, and taxed at, the partner level. The LP is not subject to entity-level corporate income tax, but it is treated as a registrant/person for GST/HST and QST purposes. Non-resident partners are taxable only on their Canadian-source partnership allocations, subject to limitation-of-benefits and treaty provisions. No tax-exempt zone status applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box entity classification election exists in Canadian law; partnership status as a flow-through vehicle is mandatory. Available statutory elections are limited to: voluntary GST/HST/QST registration before the C$30,000 small-supplier threshold is exceeded; the election under subsection 156(1) of the Excise Tax Act to treat closely related registrants as a single GST/HST registrant where the common ownership test is met; and corresponding provincial elections where Revenu Québec recognizes the federal grouping treatment. Hybrid-mismatch provisions in the Income Tax Act and Quebec taxation statutes apply automatically and cannot be overridden by entity classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) — Goods and Services Tax at 5% federal rate plus Quebec Sales Tax at 9.5%; Quebec does not participate in the Harmonized Sales Tax, so the combined headline indirect tax is 14.5%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: registration is mandatory when a supplier's worldwide taxable supplies exceed C$30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over the previous four consecutive calendar quarters; the threshold includes zero-rated export supplies, including wholesale ophthalmic frames. QST: the same C$30,000 small-supplier threshold generally applies to taxable supplies made in Quebec; registrants below the threshold may register voluntarily. A foreign LP making taxable supplies from a Canadian business platform in Quebec may be required to register even in the absence of a domestic physical establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently mandate real-time transaction clearance, fiscal stamping or government pre-approval of invoices. Registrants must issue tax-compliant electronic or paper invoices containing the supplier's name, Business Number and QST registration number, recipient details, date, description of goods, and either the tax charged or an explicit zero-rating statement. Electronic invoices in EDI, PDF or XML are accepted. GST/HST and QST returns above prescribed revenue thresholds must be filed electronically. Export evidence and underlying business records must be retained for at least six years for audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for supplies of tangible personal property, including acetate optical frames, that are exported from Canada as part of a continuous journey to a destination outside Canada, or mailed/shipped by common carrier to a foreign destination. The supplier must be registered and hold contemporaneous evidence of export. Ancillary services performed in respect of the exported goods and supplied to a non-resident person may also be zero-rated where the statutory conditions are met. Merely selling goods to a non-resident without physical export from Canada does not qualify. The LP may claim input tax credits and GST/HST/QST refunds attributable to export zero-rated supplies in the same return in which the 0% rate is applied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Completed commercial invoice describing the ophthalmic frames, HS code and sales value
Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or approved electronic export report) where required, generally for consignments valued above C$2,000 or controlled goods
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill showing the Canadian LP as consignor, a non-Canadian consignee and a destination outside Canada
Proof of export from Canada Border Services Agency or destination-country customs entry record/importation stamp
Freight forwarder delivery order and warehouse movement records evidencing the continuous international shipment
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank payment confirmation proving FX repatriation within the 180-day invoice cycle
Intercompany or sales contract, purchase order and insurance documents corroborating the export transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are an audit priority for CRA and Revenu Québec. If goods have not actually left Canada, or if the required export documentation is incomplete, the 0% rate is retrospectively reversed and the LP must remit 14.5% combined GST/QST on the supply value, plus statutory interest compounded daily. Associated input tax credits and refunds are clawed back. Administrative penalties may be imposed for false statements, omissions, gross negligence and wilful evasion under the Excise Tax Act, Quebec Tax Administration Act and related customs legislation. The normal four-year reassessment window may be extended indefinitely where a misrepresentation is attributable to neglect, carelessness or fraud. Criminal prosecution for wilful tax evasion may result in fines and imprisonment. The general partner and limited partners may also face joint and several liability for unremitted indirect taxes to the extent of LP assets and under applicable partnership and civil-liability rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central bank and monetary authority; the foreign-exchange framework is governed by the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Canada maintains no separate foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully freely convertible on both capital and current accounts. There are no statutory exchange controls, no differential treatment for capital versus current transactions, and no requirement for central-bank approval of profit remittances or dividend distributions. Profits of a Quebec Limited Partnership may be distributed to non-resident partners without currency licensing, provided the general partner has complied with partnership taxation filings and any applicable withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada). Large wire transfers and monetary remittances are subject only to FINTRAC reporting thresholds and bank-level source-of-funds due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender rules in Canada. Exporters are not required to repatriate, convert, or surrender foreign-currency export proceeds, and they may lawfully retain such proceeds in Canadian or offshore bank accounts. The only compliance obligations are reporting-related: financial institutions must report international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC, and physical cross-border currency movements of CAD 10,000 or more require corresponding declaration.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as auxiliary clearing vehicles, medium as primary treasury bank accounts. Canadian-regulated fintech and EMI equivalents (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, dLocal) can operate only as money service businesses, not as banks; they must be registered with FINTRAC and comply with provincial money-services licensing. They are suitable for Platform_Pay rail collection, supplier disbursements, and low-value cross-border settlements, but cannot provide credit, commercial letters of credit, or full FX hedging. All platform-pay balances serving as treasury assets should be swept to a Tier 1 Canadian chartered bank account to reduce custodial and liquidity risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Quebec does not impose a statutory requirement that all directors or partners appear physically in a bank branch. Remote onboarding is legally permissible through video-identity verification, digital signatures, and notarized entity documents. In practice, Tier 1 Canadian banks may require at least one Canadian-resident authorized signatory, typically a director of the corporate general partner, to attend an initial in-person or notarized verification. For a Quebec Limited Partnership, the general partner must maintain a registered office in Quebec; the financial institution will ordinarily require that the general partner's certificate, partnership agreement, and beneficial-ownership declarations be notarized by a Canadian notary before account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners with an opaque ownership or control chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the notarized limited partnership agreement, certificate of general partner status, register of partners, and a completed beneficial-ownership schedule identifying every individual owning 25% or more of the partnership. Supplement with passport copies, proof of residential address, corporate registry extracts from the jurisdiction of formation, and a narrative commercial rationale letter explaining the distribution of acetate optical frames and the Canadian wholesale business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential exposure to sanctioned jurisdictions or politically exposed persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver board- or partner-level attestations confirming no sanctioned counterparties, combined with OFAC/OSFI sanctions-screening results, entity and individual watchlist screening, and a supplier/customer ledger for the first six months. If raw-material or frame suppliers reside in a high-risk jurisdiction, provide transactional documentary evidence such as invoices, letters of credit, contracts, and customs declarations that establish the trade is bona fide and permitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient or inconsistent source of funds for the LP capital subscription.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a source-of-funds and source-of-wealth dossier for all contributing limited partners, including six to twelve months of bank statements from the remitting bank, evidence of underlying business activity, audited or reviewed financial statements, tax returns, and notarized confirmation that the funds are not derived from criminal activity. For capital injections above CAD 250,000, a chartered accountant's source-of-wealth letter materially improves bank underwriting acceptance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared business activity and actual transaction pattern under ISIC 4646.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a current sales-and-purchase contract file, proforma invoices, bill-of-lading or airway-bill samples, insurance certificates, Canada Border Services Agency import/export documentation, and an annual projection of turnover. Clearly label each wire with invoice or contract identifiers, and register the LP's business purpose with Revenu Quebec as wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames to reduce bank suspicion.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from non-resident partners should be routed through SWIFT MT103 into the LP's Tier 1 Canadian CAD account using the general partner's name and partnership registration number. There is no CAD conversion obligation and no central-bank approval; the bank will require a completed FINTRAC-compliant client remittance form for wires equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000. Field 70 should specify 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / LP SUBSCRIPTION' and, where possible, include the partnership's agreement reference. For USD inflows, funds may be credited to a USD clearing account and hedged or converted when needed. Canadian banks will conduct source-of-funds checks; the LP should attach its capital call notices and bank statements of each remitting partner to accelerate acceptance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for wholesale optical frames can be executed through SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for high-value purchases, or documentary commercial letters of credit under UCP600 where bank-confirmed trade security is required. The clearing rails include the Canadian Payments Association (now Payments Canada) for domestic CAD clearing, SWIFT for international wires, and CLS for FX settlements. For smaller platform-pay disbursements, commercial payment processors can fund supplier payouts via virtual accounts; all outbound wires must reference the underlying invoice number and must be reported by the bank if they meet the FINTRAC threshold of CAD 10,000 or more.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD and CAD/EUR deliverable outright forward contracts with a Tier 1 Canadian chartered bank or OSFI-regulated dealer
Cross-currency swaps between CAD and USD or CAD and EUR, including floating-to-fixed structures
FX options and collars on liquid convertible pairs

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be used only for exposures to restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies, and only if the bank's credit and compliance committee approves the counterparty and underlying trade

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of the anniversary of the partnership's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 150 for legal persons and partnerships; persistent default triggers administrative strike-off and loss of limited-liability protection for partners during the default period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500, plus administrative fines if partners' income is misreported

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Partnership Information Return (Form TP-600 / Relevé 19)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties from CAD 50 to CAD 500 per month, plus interest; additional fines for missing partner slips

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under Quebec or federal law for a limited partnership; audit is not statutory. A review engagement or audit may be imposed by the partnership agreement, lender covenants, or if the partnership becomes a reporting issuer.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP — IFRS or ASPE as adopted by CPA Canada; most private partnerships apply ASPE unless otherwise required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual declaration to REQ confirms the identity and control of the partnership's general partners and any limited partner holding a significant controlling interest (generally 25% or more of partnership interests). Any transfer of partnership interests that changes the composition of general partners or triggers a control change must be reported to REQ within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Dossier commun / Register of Partners with names, addresses, contributions, and profit-sharing ratios
Register of directors of the general partner (when the general partner is a legal entity)
Minute book containing partnership agreements, resolutions, and transfer records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 200 – 400 (approximately USD 150 – 300) per year for a registered office/agent in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by statute; if lender-required, review engagement CAD 3,000 – 8,000 (USD 2,200 – 6,000), full audit CAD 12,000 – 25,000 (USD 9,000 – 18,500)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (combined federal 15% general corporate income tax and Quebec 11.5% general corporate tax; the LP itself is fiscally transparent and does not pay tax, allocated income is taxed in partners' hands)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level tax for the limited partnership; eligible corporate partners may use the federal 13% general reduction, the Quebec small-business deduction (3.2%) on CAD 500,000 active business income, SR&ED refundable tax credits, Quebec innovation/design tax credits, and accelerated capital cost allowances for manufacturing equipment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (Canada Revenue Agency) — filed electronically via CRA 'My Business Account' or GIFI / Revenu Québec E-services
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period end; fiscal period ending December 31 generally due March 31 of the following calendar year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name and address of the limited partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact registered name under Quebec Enterprise Registrar; disclose foreign place of effective management if any.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Canada Revenue Agency business number (BN) of the partnership (15 characters)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must use a deemed business number by contacting CRA; do not use the general partner's BN.
Aligned to calendar year for simplicity; for non-resident partners, an optional non-calendar period may affect treaty timing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership type indicator (Limited Partnership) and applicable statute
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate 'Limited' and identify the province of formation (Quebec).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of each partner's income/loss, foreign-source income, and tax credits to T5013 slips
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, allocate only Canadian-source business income attributable to its permanent establishment in Quebec; disclose tax residency and bilateral treaty position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Existence of non-arm's-length transactions and foreign ownership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form T106 for any transaction with a non-resident related party exceeding CAD 1,000,000 aggregated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T5013: CAD 25 per day per partner, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per partnership return; false or incomplete returns may trigger severe criminal and administrative penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Relevé 15 (RL-15) — Revenu Québec; transmitted via 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' (Clic Revenu portal)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The last day of February following the calendar year in which the partnership's fiscal period ends

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner's name and address, and Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) of the partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the partner's foreign address and tax jurisdiction; non-residents need no Quebec NEQ but may be registered for tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner's social insurance number, business number or 'NR' marker
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert 'NR' followed by the country of residence; Quebec issues a deemed registration number if none exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of Canadian-source business income allocated from the Quebec permanent establishment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Quebec-source portion attributable to the LP's commercial activity in Quebec is reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income allocated (if any), including foreign exchange gains
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners typically report foreign-source income in their own residence country; Quebec will not assess it unless treaty allows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Investment income, withholding taxes, and tax credits allocated to the partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, a separate summary must state Part XIII withholding paid on any passive income such as interest or royalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late RL-15: CAD 100 minimum plus CAD 25 per day, maximum CAD 2,500; additional penalties up to 5% of unreported amounts; and prosecution for false representation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding rate on dividends paid to a non-resident (Income Tax Act s.212(2)); limited partnership profit allocations of active business income are not treated as dividends and remain taxable in the partner's hands, subject to treaty allocation rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced treaty rates, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the payer/withholding agent the applicable CRA form (NR301 for dividends/ownership structure, NR302 for interest or royalties), attach an original or digitally certified tax residency certificate (TRC), and provide a declaration of beneficial ownership before payment. Reduced rates commonly: 5% for dividends where the beneficial owner holds at least 10% of the voting shares in the Canadian payer, 15% for portfolio dividends; 10% or lower for interest; 10% or 0% for royalties depending on IP character and Canada's DTAs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates are 25% for interest (subject to arm's-length exemption under s.212(3)(b)) and 25% for royalties. Treaty-reduced rates under typical Canada DTAs (e.g., Canada-US, Canada-France, Canada-UK) are 10% for interest and royalties; certain copyright and software royalties may be 0% under protocol carve-outs.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate non-arm's-length transactions with a single non-resident in one taxation year triggers the Form T106 filing requirement; contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation (OECD-compliant local/master elements) is expected where the LP is part of a MNE group with gross revenues exceed CAD 5,000,000 or has cross-border related party distribution/wholesale transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute; however, ITA s.245 General Anti-Avoidance Rule and Quebec's analogous GAAR require real commercial substance and for the partnership to have permanent establishment capacity, active risk management, and demonstrable business purpose. A limited partnership with no employees, no premises, and all decisions made outside Quebec is vulnerable to re-characterization of its Canadian-source income as passive royalties and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting allocated LP income from T5013/RL-15, creating false bookkeeping for acetate frame sales, destroying records, or understating Quebec-source wholesale revenues.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal ITA penalties of 50% to 200% of evaded tax, criminal fines up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; Revenu Québec may levy civil penalties of 90% to 200% and proceed with criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers of the general partner are jointly and severally liable for remittance failures and civil restitution; serious cases trigger court orders freezing personal assets, seizure of passports and travel bans, and up to 5 years imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling eyewear frames to a related off-shore distributor without contemporaneous functional/risk analysis; failing to file Form T106 where non-arm's-length transactions exceed CAD 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can reprice the transactions and charge 10% penalty on the net transfer-pricing adjustment; late T106 filing penalty of CAD 24 per day up to CAD 2,400; interest accrues on additional tax assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: In a limited partnership corporate general partner, directors can be liable for the 10% penalty if they knowingly directed, participated in, or acquiesced in the non-compliance; cross-border advisory fee sharing taints directors' bonus and indemnity claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the Quebec LP merely as a flow-through acquisition vehicle with no physical warehousing, no managerial staff, no inventory-holding in Quebec, and CUP-neutral invoices sent to an offshore master within a tax-haven jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR (ITA s.245) and Quebec GAAR permit revenue authorities to ignore the entity or allocation; treaty benefits may be denied and the entire distribution recharacterized as royalties subject to 25% Part XIII withholding, plus 50% misrepresentation penalty under s.163(2).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who structure the scheme may be jointly liable for the corporation's tax plus promoter penalties; CRA can issue a 'tax avoidance' compliance order, prohibit the director from leaving Canada, and seize corporate and personal records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold on Non-Resident Partner Allocations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profit shares to an offshore limited partner without advising CRA/Revenu Québec, without filing NR4 forms, or without withholding Part XIII tax on passive-source income elements such as interest and royalties embedded in the allocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Part XIII withholding failure triggers a penalty equal to 10% (first occurrence) or 20% (subsequent occurrence) of the unremitted amount under ITA s.227(9), plus interest; Quebec civil demand for the unpaid withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner are personally liable under ITA s.227.1 for the full amount of unremitted Part XIII taxes, plus Revenu Québec allows recovery against personal assets; bank support and travel permits can be refused until payment in full.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting settlement for optical frame exports through non-bank 'platform pay' intermediaries to a Cayman-owned trading subsidiary without customer due diligence, transaction records, or FINTRAC reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties of up to CAD 1,000,000 for corporations (and implicitly of officers) and CAD 100,000 for individuals; Quebec's anti-money-laundering statutes also impose disciplinary licence consequences; criminal confiscation could follow the commercial transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly use unregulated rails to evade Canadian tax or sanctions are subject to personal fines up to CAD 500,000, disgorgement of profits, imprisonment up to 5 years, and travel prohibition under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
